narrative:
The model estimates a 70% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile that, according to patterns learned from many similar employees, strongly signal higher turnover risk.

The most influential factor is your relatively short overall career experience of 1-5 years. Most employees the model expects to stay have either 6-10 years or more than 11 years of total experience, so your limited tenure pulls the prediction noticeably toward leaving. The second strongest driver is that you have received other job offers while working here. Having external opportunities is a clear push toward departure, as the model has learned that people in your situation often choose to move on. Finally, your time in this current organization (also 1-5 years) adds further weight in the same direction, since longer tenure at one employer is more common among those predicted to remain.

Taken together, these three factors outweighed many positive elements such as having medical insurance and working in the medical sector. The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you and exploring whether additional training, clearer promotion paths, or better recognition could increase your sense of stability and commitment. You may also want to reflect on whether the external opportunities align with your long-term plans. Addressing these areas could help shift the outlook in the future.
